purpose: Answer keys and inputs for P15 part 2: how often US adults spend time in person with each kind of tie, how many hours make a friend, and how closeness fades without contact. Real rates check totals; they never pick one person's contact.

sources.citation: General Social Survey 1972-2024 Cumulative Datafile, Release 3, SDA codebook (sda.berkeley.edu/sdaweb/docs/gss24rel3/DOC/hcbk0040.htm): "How often do you spend a social evening with ...", pooled over the years asked, percent of valid answers.
categories: once or twice a week (several times a week for parents and siblings)
sources.limits: A social evening, not any meeting; not restricted to relatives living elsewhere; pooled years.

sources.citation: Kannan and Veazie (2022), US trends in social isolation, social engagement, and companionship, SSM Population Health 21:101331, using the American Time Use Survey 2003-2020 (219,368 respondents 15 and older): average minutes per day in the presence of each group.
sources.limits: Not asked for sleep, grooming or work. 'Others' includes roommates, neighbors, acquaintances, coworkers and clients.

sources.citation: Hall (2019), How many hours does it take to make a friend?, Journal of Social and Personal Relationships 36(4), doi:10.1177/0265407518761225; University of Kansas release, March 6, 2018.
sources.findings: Roughly 50 hours from acquaintance to casual friend, 90 hours to friend and more than 200 hours to close friend; combined across both studies 40-60, 80-100 and more than 200 hours. Hours spent working together count less than time socializing.
sources.limits: Release figures; the article's coefficients were not read.

sources.citation: Roberts and Dunbar (2015), Managing relationship decay, Human Nature 26(4):426-450.
sources.findings: 25 students followed for 18 months across leaving school: emotional closeness to kin rose (b = 0.27) while closeness to friends fell (b = -0.62); 70.3% of inner-layer kin stayed inner-layer against 48.6% of friends. Contact frequency held women's friendships; shared activity held men's.
sources.limits: The paper reports no half-life. The 18- and 36-month half-lives in P15 come from the P13 director, not this paper.

sources.citation: Pew Research Center (January 25, 2024), Young adults' relationship with their parents, adults 18 to 34 about the parent they communicate with most, excluding a parent they live with.
sources.findings: 22% see that parent in person at least a few times a week; 35% a few times a month or once a month; 42% less than once a month, including 6% never.

sources.citation: Pew Research Center (February 21, 2006), Families drawn together by communication revolution, 2005 survey.
sources.findings: 56% of adults whose parent lives in the same town see or talk to that parent every day, against 22% when the parent lives in a different town (any contact, phone included).
